findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the feature-flag check meaningless
findings.body: The helper reads the FlagSqlExpressions toggle, negates it, and then returns false on both branches, so it is hard-coded to false regardless of the flag. The flag check at the call site in ReadQuery therefore never does anything useful. The disable is intended, but the code reads as if it honours the flag. Anyone who later edits one branch could unintentionally re-enable SQL expressions. The helper should be replaced with an explicit unconditional rejection, with a comment stating that SQL expressions are disabled for the security fix.

findings.title: No test covers the new SQL-disabled rejection path
findings.body: The PR changes ReadQuery so that QueryTypeSQL always returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', but no test was added or updated to assert this. Without a test, a future change that re-enables the path (for example by fixing enableSqlExpressions) would not be caught. A regression test should assert that a SQL query is rejected with and without the feature flag enabled.

findings.title: NoData result is unconditionally overwritten by TableData
findings.body: When frame.Rows() == 0, rsp.Values is set to NoData, but the next statement unconditionally reassigns rsp.Values to TableData. The NoData branch is dead code, so empty SQL results are always returned as TableData. This is pre-existing and not introduced by the PR, but it sits in the same Execute function being edited here and should be fixed (for example with an else).
